law.DEADLINE: Hospitals can’t set a time limit for applying for financial assistance.
law.ASSETS: Hospitals can’t count your savings or other assets when deciding if you qualify.
law.INCOME_PROOF: Hospitals can only ask for recent pay stubs or tax returns as proof of income.
law.CREDIT_REPORTING: Hospitals can’t report this kind of medical debt to credit agencies.
law.LIENS: If you qualify for charity or discount care, the hospital can’t put a lien on your home or other real property to collect.
law.MEDICAL_FIRST: Hospitals can’t make you apply for Medi-Cal or other coverage before they’ll consider you.

audit.introShort: We compared each hospital’s policy with six California rules.
audit.what1: No deadline to apply for financial help.
audit.what2: No test of savings or other assets.
audit.what3: Proof of income limited to pay stubs or tax returns.
audit.what4: No reporting of medical debt to credit agencies.
audit.what5: No liens on the homes of patients who qualify for help.
audit.what6: Patients can’t be required to apply for Medi-Cal first.
audit.heroAll: We checked every California hospital’s rules for helping patients.
audit.heroSf: We checked San Francisco hospitals’ rules for helping patients.

audit.endH: Got a bill from a California hospital? Check it in a minute.
why.DEADLINE: California says there can be no deadline to apply for help.
why.ASSETS: California says hospitals can’t count your savings when you ask for help.
why.INCOME_PROOF: California says a pay stub or tax return is enough proof of income.
why.CREDIT_REPORTING: California says hospitals can’t report medical debt to credit bureaus.
why.LIENS: California says hospitals can’t put a lien on the home of a patient who qualifies for help.
why.MEDICAL_FIRST: California says hospitals can’t make you apply for Medi-Cal first.
landing.lead: Snap your ER bill. We check every line and tell you what you really owe.
landing.trust2: Nothing is sent without your approval
landing.problemH: Medical debt is common. Help is often hidden.
landing.stat1: About 20 million people in the US owe medical debt.
landing.stat2: California’s Attorney General warned that hospitals were failing to tell patients about free and discounted care.
landing.stat3: One California hospital agreed to contact about 43,000 former patients about refunds.
landing.stat4: We checked the policies of 470 California hospitals. 14 conflict with state law, and 47 more likely do.
landing.step1: Take a photo of your itemized ER bill. A clear photo is all we need.
landing.step2: We compare each charge to the prices your hospital publishes.
landing.step3: You see each mistake and what it costs you.
landing.step4: Who lives with you, your income, and your insurance. That’s it.
landing.step5T: You see what you really owe
landing.step5: One plain answer, and the rule behind it.
landing.step6: Read them, approve them, and send them yourself.
landing.qAsk: How many people live in your home, counting you?
landing.qHelp: This decides which free-care rules apply.
landing.meter: Your income is 125% of the federal poverty level. Free care covers up to 138%.
landing.why: Your household income is 125% of the federal poverty level. ZSFG gives free care up to 138%, under California’s charity care law.
landing.letterRe: Re: Charity care and a corrected bill
landing.letterP1: I am asking for free care under your charity care policy. My household income is 125% of the federal poverty level.
landing.letterP2: Please also remove the duplicate CBC charge on line 6.
landing.letterCheck: I read this letter and it is correct
landing.letterNote: You send it yourself. Recount never contacts the hospital for you.
landing.lupaSub: Lupa answers questions about your bill. Lupa explains. You decide.

landing.q1: Why was the blood test charged twice?
landing.a1: Lines 5 and 6 are the same test, a CBC with platelets, on the same day, at $269 each. That is usually a billing mistake. Your letter asks the hospital to remove one, which saves $269.
landing.finalH: Check your bill before you pay it.
landing.finalP: Have your ER bill ready. We do the reading.
